questions.question: At a certain sum of money with the interest rate of 6% per annum for 4 years. the simple interest is Rs. 4500. Find the compound interest (compounding annually) of 2 years at the same sum when the rate of interest is 4% per annum,
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Rate₁ = 6%

Time₁ = 4 years

Simple Interest = Rs. 4500

Time₂ = 2 years

Rate₂ = 4%

**Concept Used:**

Simple Interest = PRT/100

Compound Interest = P(1 + R/100)T - P

**Calculation:**

Simple Interest = PRT/100

4500 = (P × 6 × 4)/100

P = (4500 × 100)/(6 × 4)

P = 750 × 25

P = Rs. 18750

Compound Interest = P(1 + R/100)T - P

Compound Interest = 18750(1 + 4/100)² - 18750

Compound Interest = 18750(26/25)2 - 18750

Compound Interest = 18750 × 676/625 - 18750 

Compound Interest = 20280 - 18750 

Compound Interest = 1530

**∴ Option 1 is the correct answer.**

questions.question: The cost of diamond is directly proportional to the square of its weight. The cost of diamond is Rs. 87880. It break into two pieces whose weight are in the ratio of 5 ∶ 8. What is the loss incurred because of the breakage?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The cost of a diamond is directly proportional to the square of its weight.

Cost of the diamond = Rs. 87880

Weight ratio after breakage = 5 ∶ 8

**Formula Used:**

Let the total weight of the diamond be w.

Cost ∝ Weight²

Cost = k × Weight²

**Calculation:**

Let the weights of the two pieces be 5x and 8x.

Total weight = 5x + 8x = 13x

Initial cost = k × (13x)²

⇒ 87880 = k × (13x)²

⇒ k = 87880 / 169x²

Cost of the first piece = k × (5x)²

Cost of the second piece = k × (8x)²

⇒ k × (5x)² = (87880 / 169x²) × 25x²

Cost of the first piece = (87880 × 25) / 169

Cost of the first piece = Rs. 13000

⇒ k × (8x)² = (87880 / 169x²) × 64x²

Cost of the second piece = (87880 × 64) / 169

Cost of the second piece = Rs. 33280

Total cost after breakage = Rs. 13000 + Rs. 33280 = Rs. 46280

Loss incurred = Initial cost - Total cost after breakage

Loss incurred = Rs. 87880 - Rs. 46280

Loss incurred = Rs. 41600

**The loss incurred because of the breakage is Rs. 41600.**

questions.question: P is 30% more efficient than Q. How much time will they, working together, take to complete a job that P alone could have done in 23 days?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

P is 30% more efficient than Q.

P alone could complete the job in 23 days.

**Formula Used:**

Work Efficiency Ratio: P:Q = 130:100 = 13:10

Combined work rate = Work rate of P + Work rate of Q

Time taken to complete the work together = Total work / Combined work rate

**Calculation:**

Let the total work be W.

Work rate of P = W / 23

Work rate of Q = W / 23 × (10/13)

Combined work rate = W / 23 + W / 23 × (10/13)

Combined work rate = W / 23 × (1 + 10/13)

Combined work rate = W / 23 × 23/13

questions.question: Three friends A, B and C start running around a circular stadium and complete a single round in 24 seconds, 36 seconds and 30 seconds, respectively. After how many minutes will they meet again at the starting point ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time taken to meet again at the starting point = LCM of individual times taken by each person.

⇒ LCM of 24, 36 and 30 seconds = 360 seconds.

⇒ Convert time into minutes = 360 ÷ 60 = 6 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/605c7e51d63bb3b319e97ae9499fc776dd50c03f8ed39498ed9095035fdc426a.png] 

**Given:**

Time taken by A to complete a round = 24 seconds

Time taken by B to complete a round = 36 seconds

Time taken by C to complete a round = 30 seconds

**Formula Used:**

Time after which they meet at the starting point = LCM of individual times.

**Calculation:**

⇒ Prime factorisation of 24 = 2³ × 3

⇒ Prime factorisation of 36 = 2² × 3²

⇒ Prime factorisation of 30 = 2 × 3 × 5

⇒ LCM (24, 36, 30) = Highest powers of all prime factors = 2³ × 3² × 5

⇒ LCM = 8 × 9 × 5 = 360 seconds

⇒ We know that 1 minute = 60 seconds

⇒ Time in minutes = 360 ÷ 60 = 6 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 6 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Meeting at the Starting Point

When multiple runners run on a circular track, the time after which they all meet simultaneously at the starting point is always the LCM of the times taken by each runner to complete one full round.

Meeting Anywhere on the Track for the First Time

If two runners start running simultaneously from the exact same point, they will meet for the first time anywhere on the track after Time = Track Length ÷ Relative Speed.

Relative Speed on a Circular Track

When moving in the same direction, relative speed = a − b. When moving in opposite directions, relative speed = a + b.

questions.question: The mean proportional of 4a² and x is (1)/(5a) where a is a positive number, then the value of x is ____.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For any continuous proportion, the square of the mean proportional is equal to the product of the first and third terms.

⇒ (1 / 5a)² = 4a² × x

⇒ 1 / 25a² = 4a² × x

⇒ x = 1 / 100a⁴

**∴ The correct answer is 1 / (100a⁴).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First term = 4a²

Mean proportional = 1 / (5a)

Third term = x

**Formula Used:**

Mean Proportional = √(First Term × Third Term)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5d6a0aa2ef30fd4ab8da488ae95ef28b9b3213da2b178ca53e33d7ab1dd99fd9.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 1 / (5a) = √(4a² × x)

⇒ Squaring both sides, we get:

⇒ [1 / (5a)]² = 4a² × x

⇒ 1 / (25a²) = 4a² × x

⇒ x = 1 / (25a² × 4a²)

⇒ x = 1 / (100a⁴)

**∴ The correct answer is 1 / (100a⁴).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional

For two given numbers a and b, the mean proportional x is calculated as x = √(a × b). It serves as the geometric mean between the two values in a continued proportion.

Third Proportional

For two numbers a and b, the third proportional c satisfies the continued proportion a : b :: b : c. It is calculated directly using the formula c = b² / a.

Fourth Proportional

For three distinct numbers a, b, and c, the fourth proportional d completes the standard proportion a : b :: c : d, yielding the formula d = (b × c) / a.

Compound Ratio

When two or more distinct ratios are multiplied together term by term (for example, a:b and c:d merge into ac:bd), the resulting combined ratio is known as a compound ratio.
</p

questions.question: A thief noticed a policeman at a distance of 600 metres. The thief started running and the policeman chased him. The thief and policeman are running at speeds of 12 km/h and 15 km/h, respectively. Find the time (in minutes) required for the policeman to catch the thief.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed (same direction) = 15 − 12 = 3 km/h.

Initial Distance = 600 m = 0.6 km.

Time = Distance ÷ Relative speed = 0.6 ÷ 3 = 0.2 hours.

Time in minutes = 0.2 × 60 = 12 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance between Policeman and Thief (D) = 600 m = 0.6 km

Speed of Policeman (Sₚ) = 15 km/h

Speed of Thief (Sₜ) = 12 km/h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/092ea22a3f1907faa90a5b0f256bb4a61651f22bebfa96459a6581118f1be98b.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (when moving in the same direction) = Sₚ − Sₜ

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative Speed = 15 km/h − 12 km/h = 3 km/h

⇒ Time required to catch the thief = 0.6 km ÷ 3 km/h

⇒ Time = 0.2 hours

⇒ Time in minutes = 0.2 × 60 = 12 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 12 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction)

When two objects move towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂.

Average Speed

Average speed is the total distance traveled divided by the total time taken. For two equal distances covered at speeds x and y, Average Speed = 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply the value by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

questions.question: If K + 3, k + 2, 3k – 7, 2k – 3 are in proportion in the given order, then what will be the minimum value of the fourth proportion?
questions.solution:
**Given**

K + 3, k + 2, 3k – 7, 2k – 3 

**Calculation**

⇒ K + 3/k + 2 = 3k – 7/2k – 3 

⇒ (K + 3)(2k – 3) = (k + 2)(3k - 7)

⇒ 2k² - 3k + 6k -9 = 3k² - 7k + 6k - 14

⇒ k2 - 4k - 5 = 0

⇒ (K + 1)(k – 5)

⇒ (K + 1) = 0 or (k – 5) = 0

⇒ k = -1 or K = 5

Since minimum value is asked we will consider k = -1

The fourth proportional = 2k - 3 = -2 - 3 = -5

**The answer is -5.**

questions.question: The cost price of an article 'A' is 42.85% of the marked price of the article 'A'. If the article is sold at the discount of Rs.100, then the profit percentage earned on the article 'A' is 50%. If the selling price of the article is Rs. 5.625x, then find the value of (x)⁽³/⁵⁾

Fractional value of 42.85% is 3/7. Let MP = 7 units, then CP = 3 units.

Profit = 50% ⇒ SP = 3 × 1.5 = 4.5 units.

Discount = MP − SP = 7 − 4.5 = 2.5 units.

2.5 units = ₹100 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹40 ⇒ SP = 4.5 × 40 = ₹180.

Now, 5.625x = 180 ⇒ (45/8)x = 180 ⇒ x = 32.

Value of x³/⁵ = (32)³/⁵ = (2⁵)³/⁵ = 2³ = 8.

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) is 42.85% of Marked Price (MP).

Discount = ₹100

Profit percentage = 50%

Selling Price (SP) = 5.625x

**Formula Used:**

SP = CP + Profit

SP = MP − Discount

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ac257b97195492eb37b6f4348a39bfd23a62972dc2b034c3f6a1a6fc037075ef.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Fraction equivalent of 42.85% = 3/7

⇒ Let CP = 3a and MP = 7a

⇒ Profit = 50% of CP = 50/100 × 3a = 1.5a

⇒ SP = CP + Profit = 3a + 1.5a = 4.5a

⇒ Discount = MP − SP = 7a − 4.5a = 2.5a

⇒ 2.5a = 100

⇒ a = 100 ÷ 2.5 = 40

⇒ SP = 4.5 × 40 = ₹180

Given SP = 5.625x, so equating both values:

⇒ 5.625 × x = 180

⇒ (45/8) × x = 180

⇒ x = (180 × 8) ÷ 45 = 32

Finding the value of x³/⁵:

⇒ (32)³/⁵ = (2⁵)³/⁵ = 2³ = 8

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

questions.question: A mango juice is made by mixing water and mango concentrate in the ratio 9 : 7. If x litres of water and 3x litres of mango concentrate is mixed in 160 litres of mango juice, then the new ratio becomes 13 : 14. What is the quantity of the new mango juice (in litres)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Initial Water = 160 × (9/16) = 90 L, Initial Mango = 160 × (7/16) = 70 L.

After adding x L water and 3x L mango concentrate, the ratio becomes 13 : 14.

⇒ (90 + x) / (70 + 3x) = 13 / 14

⇒ 1260 + 14x = 910 + 39x ⇒ 25x = 350 ⇒ x = 14.

Total new quantity = Initial + Added = 160 + x + 3x = 160 + 4(14) = 216 L.

**∴ The correct answer is 216 litres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6a6f67128abfed30430633093a28bd334805628b9214b505d2d0418771f3cc9f.png] 

**Given:**

Total volume of initial mango juice = 160 litres

Ratio of water to mango concentrate = 9 : 7

**Calculations:**

⇒ Quantity of water initially = (9 / 16) × 160 = 90 litres

⇒ Quantity of mango concentrate initially = (7 / 16) × 160 = 70 litres

After adding x litres of water and 3x litres of mango concentrate:

⇒ New quantity of water = (90 + x) litres

⇒ New quantity of mango concentrate = (70 + 3x) litres

According to the given condition, the new ratio is 13 : 14.

⇒ (90 + x) / (70 + 3x) = 13 / 14

⇒ 14 × (90 + x) = 13 × (70 + 3x)

⇒ 1260 + 14x = 910 + 39x

⇒ 39x − 14x = 1260 − 910

⇒ 25x = 350

⇒ x = 14

Total new quantity of mango juice = Initial quantity + Added quantities

questions.question: In human body, the food passes through a continuous canal which begins at ______ and ends at anus.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is a __**buccal cavity.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The human digestive system consists of a continuous **canal** through which food passes.
 
• The **canal begins at the buccal cavity and ends at the anus.**
 
• **Human Digestion system-**
 
 
• ​The human digestive system consists of several organs and structures involved in the process of digestion.
 
• The **canal begins at the buccal cavity,** also known as the **mouth or oral cavity**, where **food enters the body.**
 
• After being chewed and mixed with **saliva**, the food is formed into a small, soft mass called a **bolus**.
 
• The bolus then passes through the pharynx, which is the junction between the buccal cavity and the esophagus.
 
• From the pharynx, the food travels down the **esophagus**, also known as the **food pipe or the gullet.**
 
• The esophagus is a muscular tube that propels food toward the stomach through rhythmic contractions called peristalsis.
 
• Once the food reaches the stomach, it undergoes further digestion through the action of **stomach acids and enzymes.**
 
• The stomach mixes the food with **gastric juices** and breaks it down into a **semi-liquid mixture called chyme.**
 
• The chyme is then gradually released into the **small intestine, the longest part of the digestive tract.**
 
• In the small intestine, the majority of nutrient **absorption **takes place, aided by specialized structures called **villi**.
 
• The small intestine consists of three sections: the **duodenum, jejunum, and ileum.**
 
• After passing through the small intestine, the remaining waste material enters the large intestine, also known as the **colon**.
 
• In the large intestine, water and electrolytes are absorbed from the waste, forming solid feces.
 
• The feces are stored in the rectum until they are eliminated from the body through the **anus** during the process of **defecation**.

__
 
• Phloem

 
 
• It is the complex tissue that acts as a transport system for soluble organic compounds within vascular plants.
 
• It transports the food made in leaves to other parts of plants.
 
• It is made up of living tissue, which uses turgor pressure and energy in the form of ATP to actively transport sugars to the plant organs

• Root hairs
 
 
• These are cylindrical extensions of root epidermal cells.
 
• The primary function is to collect water and mineral nutrients from the soil. It takes the solution up by the roots to the rest of the plant.
 
 
 
• Epiblema
 
 
• Epidermis with root hairs is called epiblema.
 
• It is composed of one layer of compactly arranged parenchymatous cells.
 
• It is usually located between the epidermis and cortex in the root or stem of a plant.
 
• The root hairs and thin-walled epiblema cells absorb water and minerals salts from the soil.

__
 
• The design and printing of currency notes and their circulation is not one of the objectives of the **NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India).**
 
• **The NITI Aayog** is a policy think tank of the Government of India that primarily focuses on strategic and long-term planning for the country's development.
 
• It acts as a platform for cooperative federalism, fostering the involvement of **states in policy formulation and implementation**.
 
• The responsibility for the design, printing, and circulation of currency notes in India lies with the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, which is the central banking institution of the country.
 
• **The RBI **is responsible for formulating and implementing monetary policy, issuing currency notes, and regulating the overall banking and financial system in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The NITI Aayog, or the National Institution for Transforming India,** is a policy think tank of the **Government of India.**
 
• It was established on** January 1, 2015**, to replace the erstwhile Planning Commission.
 
• **The NITI Aayog's primary objective **is to provide strategic and long-term policy inputs to the central and state governments to foster sustainable and inclusive development across various sectors of the Indian economy.
 
• **The key functions and objectives of the NITI Aayog include:**
 
 
• **Formulating strategic and long-term development plans: **The NITI Aayog formulates and recommends strategic plans, medium-term and long-term development frameworks, and policies for various sectors of the economy.
 
• **Cooperative federalism:** The NITI Aayog promotes cooperative federalism by fostering the involvement of state governments in policy formulation and implementation, ensuring their active participation and contribution in the planning process.
 
• **Policy research and innovation: **The NITI Aayog conducts research, analysis, and evidence-based policy studies on various social and economic issues to identify challenges, suggest innovative solutions, and provide policy recommendations to the government.
 
• **Monitoring and evaluation: **The NITI Aayog monitors and evaluates the implementation of policies and programs, assesses their outcomes, and suggests mid-course corrections, if required, to achieve desired development goals.
 
• **International cooperation: **The NITI Aayog facilitates international cooperation and exchange of best practices in policy planning and development with other countries and international organizations.
 
• **Collaborative platforms: **The NITI Aayog provides a platform for collaboration and dialogue among various stakeholders, including government agencies, experts, academicians, industry representatives, and civil society organizations, to foster participative and inclusive policy-making.
 
• It's important to note that the NITI Aayog's role is primarily advisory in nature, and the responsibility for implementing policies and executing projects lies with the respective ministries and departments of the central and state governments.

• The dance form derives its name from a village named Kuchipudi in the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh.
 
• Kuchipudi derives its roots from the ancient Hindu Sanskrit text of Natya Shastra and is a dance-drama performance.
 
• The dance drama performance has a long history in Andhra Pradesh and is known under the generic name Yakshagana.
 
• The systematized and modern version of Kuchipudi was founded by Siddhendra Yogi in the 17th century. The Kuchipudi style of Yakshagana was conceived by Yogi. He was guided by his guru Tirthanarayana Yogi.
 
• It is largely devoted to the Hindu God - Krishna and it is most closely related to Bhagavata Mela.
 
• Traditionally this dance form is performed only by male artists, later female artists were also allowed.
 
• The dance drama has the following components:
 
 
• Dharavu - a short preliminary dance performed by the artists after their roles are introduced.
 
• Nritta - it is the pure dance performance presented after the Dharavi. It includes parts viz., darus, jatis, jatiswarams, tirmanas, and tillanas.
 
• Nritya - it is the expressive part of the performance where the story is conveyed through rhythmic hand gestures. It includes padams, varnams, shabdams, and shlokas.
 
• Natya - it is performed when the underlying text is a play.

__
 
• Replace **isn't with hasn't.**
 
• The sentence and the question tag must be in the same tense. Here we need a question tag in the perfect tense.
 
• As we must use the pronoun of the subject of the given clause in the question tag. Here the subject of the given clause is Heena, so the pronoun 'she' should be used in the question tag.
 
• The sentence is positive, thus the question tag used must be negative.
 
• Hence, Option 3 is the correct answer.

**The correct sentence is:*** Heena has been working very hard for the past two years, hasn't she?*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Question tags are short questions at the end of statements.
 
• They are mainly used in speech when we want to: *confirm that something is true or not, or to encourage a reply from the person we are speaking to.*
 
• Question tags are formed with the auxiliary or modal verb from the statement and the appropriate subject.
 
• A positive statement is followed by a negative question tag.
 
 
• Jack is from Spain, isn't he?
 
• Mary can speak English, can't she?
 
 
 
• A negative statement is followed by a positive question tag.
 
 
• They aren't funny, are they?
 
• He shouldn't say things like that, should he?
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dc6860af6f4718c1889a364603433dd6c44d3897a89b139b0c1c858601cb8c19.png] 

 
• isn't को **hasn't** के साथ बदलें ।
 
• वाक्य और question tag एक ही **tense** में होने चाहिए। यहां हमें perfect tense में question tag की जरूरत है।
 
• जैसा कि हमें question tag में दिए गए clause के विषय के **pronoun **का उपयोग करना चाहिए। यहां दिए गए clause का विषय **Heena** है, इसलिए question tag में '**she**' pronoun का प्रयोग किया जाना चाहिए।
 
• वाक्य positive है, इस प्रकार प्रयुक्त question tag **negative** होना चाहिए।
